title: Vikrant Massey Just Became a Producer. His First Bet? A Love Story Set Between Bhopal and Mussoorie.
excerpt: Netflix's Musafir Cafe marks the debut of Massey's production banner Homemade Stories — and pairs him with the director of Little Things for a monsoon romance dropping July 24.
body:
There's a particular kind of Hindi love story that works best when it doesn't try too hard — when the locations do half the talking, the silences carry weight, and the characters feel like people you might actually sit next to on a train. **Vikrant Massey** has built a career on exactly that register. And now, for the first time, he's betting his own money on it.

***Musafir Cafe***, arriving on **Netflix on July 24**, is a romantic drama series based on **Divya Prakash Dubey's** beloved Hindi novel of the same name. It's also the first project from **Homemade Stories**, Massey's newly launched production banner — making this as much a personal milestone as a creative one.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=pibvzyozY7U</youtube>


## The Story

Set against the lush, rain-soaked landscapes of **Bhopal and Mussoorie**, the series follows three strangers whose lives intersect in ways none of them planned for.



> **"From *Lootera* to *A Death in the Gunj* to *Haseen Dilruba* to last year's blockbuster *12th Fail*, he's carved a space that's rare — critically respected AND commercially viable."**


Massey plays **Chander Mohan Sharma**, a man looking for a life that finally feels like his own — the kind of restless, quietly dissatisfied protagonist he does better than almost anyone in the industry. **Vedika Pinto** (last seen in *Nishaanchi*) stars as **Sudha**, determined to write her own destiny. And **Mahima Makwana** plays **Preeti**, described as the calm at the heart of the story — steady and compassionate, even when life throws its curveballs.

> "*Pyaar, pahaad aur inn musafiron ki kahaani.*" — Netflix India's announcement caption

The series is created and written by **Sharanya Rajgopal** and directed by **Ruchir Arun**, best known for helming Netflix's quietly adored **Little Things** — which means the tonal DNA here is comfort, warmth, and emotional specificity rather than melodrama. If you loved the low-key intimacy of *Little Things*, *Musafir Cafe* is being made by people who understand that register instinctively.

## Why This Matters for Massey

Vikrant Massey has had one of the most interesting trajectories in contemporary Bollywood. From *Lootera* to *A Death in the Gunj* to *Haseen Dilruba* to last year's blockbuster *12th Fail*, he's carved a space that's rare — critically respected AND commercially viable. But production is a different game entirely.

Launching **Homemade Stories** with a Netflix original is a statement of intent. The banner's name alone signals the kind of cinema Massey wants to back: intimate, rooted, handcrafted. Not a franchise play. Not an IP grab. A love story based on a Hindi-language novel, set in two Indian cities most mainstream producers would overlook.

The supporting cast adds quiet credibility: **Adil Hussain** (of *Life of Pi* and *English Vinglish* fame), **Rajeev Siddhartha**, **Loveleen Mishra**, and **Sadia Siddiqui**. Produced by **Terribly Tiny Tales (TTT)** in association with Homemade Stories — a partnership that pairs one of India's most influential digital storytelling brands with a first-time producer who understands the assignment.

## The Diaspora Angle

Here's what matters if you're watching from outside India: *Musafir Cafe* drops globally on Netflix, which means no geo-blocks, no delayed international release, no hunting for pirated links. It streams in Hindi with subtitles, and if it follows Netflix India's usual playback, expect dubs in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam as well.

For NRI audiences, this is exactly the kind of show that fills a specific gap — a contemporary Hindi romance that doesn't lean on spectacle, doesn't feature a superstar doing backflips, and actually feels like the India you remember visiting. Bhopal's old-city charm. Mussoorie's misty roads. The particular magic of meeting someone at the wrong time and knowing it anyway.

## Mark Your Calendar

**Musafir Cafe** premieres **July 24, exclusively on Netflix**. The teaser is already up, and the trailer is expected shortly. If you're in the mood for something that moves slowly, looks gorgeous, and trusts its audience to feel rather than be told what to feel — this one's worth the wait.
